extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners preparing plant patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and examining U.S. plant patent applications (35 U.S.C. 161-164), including specification, drawings, oath/declaration, examination, and compliance with UPOV denomination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability under 35 U.S.C. 161
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever invents or discovers and asexually reproduces any distinct and new variety of plant, including cultivated sports, mutants, hybrids, and newly found seedlings, other than a tuber propagated plant or a plant found in an uncultivated state, may obtain a patent therefor, subject to the conditions and requirements of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes types of plants covered (cultivated sports, mutants, hybrids, newly found seedlings if found in a cultivated state). Case law (e.g., In re Beineke) interprets the 'invents or discovers' and human-creation aspects. Plant patent provisions apply except as otherwise provided; see related citations in MPEP §1601.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of asexually propagated plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Asexually propagated plants are those that are reproduced by means other than from seeds, such as by the rooting of cuttings, by layering, budding, grafting, inarching, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plants capable of sexual reproduction are not excluded if they have also been asexually reproduced. The inventor's oath/declaration must state that the inventor has asexually reproduced the plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of tuber propagated plants
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant patent cannot be obtained for tuber propagated plants; 'tuber' is used in its narrow horticultural sense (e.g., Irish potato and Jerusalem artichoke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception arises because the propagated part is also sold as food; ensure applicant's species is not a tuber-propagated plant when determining eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'plant' for plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'plant' has been interpreted to mean 'plant' in the ordinary and accepted sense and not in the strict scientific sense and thus excludes bacteria; it does not include asexual propagating material, per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case citations (e.g., In re Arzberger; Ex parte Hibberd) support this interpretation. Use ordinary botanical meaning when evaluating claims and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invents/discovers and asexually reproduces requirement (human activity/inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor named must be the person who has invented or discovered and asexually reproduced the new and distinct variety of plant for which a patent is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beineke demonstrates that plants not created from inception by human activity or not created by the inventor/applicant may be ineligible. For newly found plants, the oath/declaration must state they were found in a cultivated area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative protection under 35 U.S.C. 101 (utility patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: An asexually reproduced plant may alternatively be protected under 35 U.S.C. 101, provided the written description requirement can be satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: J.E.M. Ag Supply holds that plant subject matter is not excluded from 35 U.S.C. 101. An application under 101 may claim the same asexually reproduced plant and associated materials/processes; consult MPEP §2105 for differences in requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer for obviousness-type double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a terminal disclaimer may be used in appropriate situations to overcome an obviousness-type double patenting rejection based on claims to the asexually reproduced plant (35 U.S.C. 101) and the same plant in an application under 35 U.S.C. 161.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims in different applications raise obviousness-type double patenting concerns, examiners and applicants should consider terminal disclaimers as an available remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent rights and term (35 U.S.C. 163)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights associated with a plant patent include rights associated with a utility patent and the 'right to exclude' with additional terms provided in 35 U.S.C. 163. A plant patent issuing from an application filed after June 7, 1995 has a term which expires 20 years after the filing date (or earlier claimed filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patent applications will be published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b). Consider effective filing date and any claimed priorities under 120/121/365(c). See MPEP §2701 for term calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of general patent rules (37 CFR 1.161)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules relating to applications for patent for other inventions or discoveries are also applicable to applications for patents for plants except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard patent practice unless specific plant-patent provisions alter the rule; references to other MPEP sections (oath, specification, drawings) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements and order of a plant application (37 CFR 1.163(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the plant application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Plant application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet; (4) Specification; (5) Drawings (in duplicate); (6) The inventor's oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed arrangement; see MPEP §1603 and the cited CFR for formatting. Failure to include required elements may lead to objections or correction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and oath/declaration content (37 CFR 1.162)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor's oath or declaration must state that the inventor has asexually reproduced the plant and, for newly found plants, must state that it was found in a cultivated area; the applicant must be the person who has invented or discovered and asexually reproduced the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Plant Patent Application Declaration form (PTO/AIA/09) may be used for applications filed on/after September 16, 2012. Joint inventors are permitted. The oath must include the averments required by 37 CFR 1.63/1.64 plus the asexual reproduction statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification: full and complete botanical disclosure (37 CFR 1.163(a),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain as full and complete a disclosure as possible of the plant and the characteristics thereof that distinguish the same over related known varieties, and its antecedents, and must particularly point out where and in what manner the variety of plant has been asexually reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a newly found plant, the specification must particularly point out the location and character of the area where the plant was discovered. Use botanical terminology and include origin/parentage and genus/species designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification sections and ordering (37 CFR 1.163(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include, in order when applicable: Title; Cross-reference to related applications; Statement regarding federally sponsored research; Latin name of genus and species; Variety denomination; Background; Brief summary; Brief description of drawing; Detailed botanical description; A single claim; Abstract of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section should be preceded by an appropriate heading in upper case; inclusion of Latin name and variety denomination facilitates registration and database compilation (see ADS usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Botanical description requirements (use botanical terms, not catalog language)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include a complete detailed description expressed in botanical terms in the general form followed in standard botanical textbooks or publications rather than a mere broad nonbotanical characterization as commonly found in nursery or seed catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include origin or parentage and genus/species; particularly point out the location/manner of asexual reproduction. Form paragraphs (e.g., 16.01, 16.09, 16.10) may be used to object if these requirements are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color disclosure requirements and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where color is a distinctive feature of the plant, the color should be positively identified in the specification by reference to a designated color as given by a recognized color dictionary or color chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 16.02 and 16.03 may be used to object to color discrepancies or non-support for colors. If drawings/photos are in color, two color copies are required; failure to include duplicates will result in required correction before examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted corrections to written description without new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the written description of a plant is deficient in certain respects, a clarification or additional description, or even a wholesale substitution of the original description so long as not totally inconsistent and unrelated to the original description and photograph may be submitted in reply to an Office action without constituting new matter under 35 U.S.C. 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Jessel v. Newland as precedent; ensure substituted description remains related to the original disclosure to avoid new matter issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit rules inapplicable to plant patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules on Deposit of Biological Materials (37 CFR 1.801-1.809) do not apply to plant patent applications in view of the reduced disclosure requirements of 35 U.S.C. 162, even where a deposit has been made in conjunction with a utility application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on biological material deposit to satisfy plant patent disclosure requirements; follow 35 U.S.C. 162 disclosure standards instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-claim requirement and claim form (37 CFR 1.164)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim shall be in formal terms to the new and distinct variety of the specified plant as described and illustrated, and may also recite the principal distinguishing characteristics. More than one claim is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A plant patent is granted only on the entire plant. A method claim in a plant patent application is improper. Example proper claim: 'A new and distinct variety of hybrid tea rose plant, substantially as illustrated and described herein.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings standards for plant patents (37 CFR 1.165; 1.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent drawings should be artistically and competently executed and must comply with the requirements of § 1.84. The drawing must disclose all the distinctive characteristics of the plant capable of visual representation. Drawings may be in color and must be in color if color is a distinguishing characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two copies of color drawings/photographs required. Drawings must meet paper type, size, margin, numbering, arrangement, and view-numbering rules; no holes; proper identification on front top margin. Forms (¶16.06, 16.07, 16.11) may be used to object to duplicity, competence, or scale issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing sheet format and procedural details
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted must be on flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny durable paper; one side only; sheet sizes limited to A4 or 8.5x11 inches; margins specified; views not superimposed; consecutive numbering of sheets/views; words left-to-right, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow paragraph (f)-(u) and related subparagraphs in 37 CFR 1.84/1.165 for exact margin sizes, sight dimensions, view numbering conventions, and handling of single view cases. Annotated and replacement sheets must be labeled per § 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens: examiner may require specimens (37 CFR 1.166)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may be required to furnish specimens of the plant, or its flower or fruit, in a quantity and at a time in its stage of growth as may be designated, for study and inspection; specimens should not be submitted unless specifically called for by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens must be properly packed and forwarded per instructions or made available for official inspection where grown. Use Form Paragraph 16.13 to require specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standards: statutory provisions and search
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant applications are subject to the same examination process as any other national application; statutory provisions regarding patentable subject matter, utility, novelty, obviousness, disclosure, and claim specificity apply (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, and 112), with the sole exception set forth in 35 U.S.C. 162.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners develop prior art via searches of patent classification and nonpatent literature and may obtain advisory reports from the Agricultural Research Service (ARS). The ARS report is advisory and placed in the file but not a printed paper in the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and evidentiary limits of ARS (Department of Agriculture) reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted by the Office to the Department of Agriculture for study and report; the report may indicate whether the variety is new and distinct over known varieties, and may embody criticisms or suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ARS report is advisory; matters within personal knowledge of ARS specialists are not sufficient basis for rejection unless supported by affidavits (37 CFR 1.104(d)(2)). Examiners may include parts of the report in Office actions at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action content and restrictions (claim/title/advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action on the application will include matters as in other patent applications; the claim language must be directed to the 'new and distinct variety of plant' (the entire plant), and the title must relate to the entire plant, not to its flower or fruit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit claims directed only to flower or fruit separate from the plant. Remove unwarranted advertising or laudatory expressions from the specification and objectionable background drawings (e.g., signs with nursery names). Examiner may amend language (e.g., insert 'tree' after 'apple'). Use form paragraphs (e.g., 16.04, 16.08) for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102/112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue requirements for plant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of a plant patent application for issue involves the same procedure as for other applications, with the exception that where there are color drawings the better one is selected to be printed in the patent. IPC symbols should be placed on the Issue Classification form. All plant patent applications should contain an abstract when allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the sharper/cleaner color drawing for printing; ensure classification and abstract inclusion. Follow standard issue processing procedures per 37 CFR 1.161.

rubrics_metrics.name: UPOV Convention and variety denomination registration
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition for receiving a plant patent it is necessary to register a variety denomination for that plant by including the denomination in the plant patent application; the examiner must evaluate the proposed denomination under UPOV Article 13 (not identical/confusingly similar; not misleading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed denomination ordinarily must be the same as registered in another UPOV member. The Latin name and variety denomination may be included in an Application Data Sheet (ADS) pursuant to 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3). Use form ¶16.05/16.05.01 to object if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority based on plant breeder’s rights application (35 U.S.C. 119(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a plant patent may rely upon an application for plant breeder’s rights filed in a WTO member country (or a foreign UPOV Contracting Party) for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(c) pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 119(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UPOV texts guarantee national treatment and right of priority; however, in many states breeders' rights laws, not patent laws, protect varieties. Examiner should handle priority claims accordingly and ensure required documentation for priority is present.
